about.budget: the four derived files together stay under 200 KB (spec §6), written as compact JSON (indented they would be about 237 KB); excerpts are capped at 240 (step), 400 (reply) and 120 (args, task) characters
about.not_recorded: {"recorded": false, "command": ...} where a trace is missing, never a number

rulings.R62: cost and latency come from the recording: the sum of the trace's proxy_calls cost_usd and ms, served again on replay; never what one run paid (spent, cost_usd) or measured locally (a record's ms)
rulings.R64: the ledger keeps input, cache-write, cache-read and output tokens apart; cache writes are priced at 1.25x and cache reads at 0.10x the input price, so prompt caching shows as a lower cost
rulings.R66: the gate stays as built (0.7 minus the 1/sqrt(n) band); with 13 tickets no engine clears it. That is the real result and is shown as it is, never adjusted

about.score: the scorer's per-run row for that ticket, copied from engine_scores.json
about.steps: each trace record in order: model (tokens, cost and ms from the matching proxy_calls entry), tool (name, args at most 120 characters; write: refused or written for label_ticket, the only write; the guard's scripted person says no, so every write here is refused), handoff (worker, task at most 120 characters, the state keys it changed), stop (max_turns) and error. The LangGraph and SDK desks log a refused write only in tool_calls: it is placed by its order there, or before the final model call, with traced: false
about.tickets: t001, t007, t061 (t061 is the prompt injection), plus t004 is the ticket whose supervisor runs looped drafter -> reviewer longest (10 reviews over the four engines); the plan named t010 (6 reviews), so t004 is shown instead
about.totals: calls, cost_usd and ms are the ledger's (R62); tokens_in is uncached input, cache_read and cache_write the cached parts (R64)
about.what: AgentTrace: the single and supervisor desks in all four engines, step by step, on a few tickets
